episode_title: 122. Macro predictions for 2023 with Wall Street veteran David Woo

recommendations.speaker: David Woo
recommendations.reasoning: China reopening will drive explosive growth in oil demand - from 12M to 14M barrels/day. Russia preparing major offensive in Ukraine will spike prices further. Current price ~84, can easily go to 100. China accounts for 40% of world base metals consumption and is 2nd largest energy consumer. Chinese New Year February 22nd will mark herd immunity.
recommendations.quote: I like the June, the June basically futures, the June 2020 is very brand futures, which I like. OK, now, right now is trading around 84. I think this baby can go to 100, OK, easily.
recommendations.position_context: Long oil futures, hedged with S&P 500 short
recommendations.catalyst_timing: China reopening, Russia offensive in next 2-3 weeks

recommendations.speaker: David Woo
recommendations.reasoning: If higher oil prices materialize from China reopening or Russia offensive, it will hurt global economy and stock market. Using as hedge against long oil position. Soft landing scenario is preposterous - market is underestimating inflation persistence and Fed hawkishness.
recommendations.quote: So I've also shorted some S&P, you know, 500 basically June futures against my long oil future, right? As a hedge, right? As a hedge. Because it becomes a relative value trade, right?
recommendations.position_context: Short as hedge against long oil position

recommendations.speaker: David Woo
recommendations.reasoning: Russia launching major offensive in Ukraine will force US/Europe to enforce stronger sanctions, sending oil prices through roof. Europe will face worst stagflation. Current consensus is long euro, but war scenario will crush European economy. ECB won't be hiking in crisis. High energy prices causing German de-industrialization.
recommendations.quote: I'm very much of that view that I think the reason why the market still doesn't get it is because there's too much goddamn propaganda going on... I'm bearish the euro... Europe is going to be damned. It's going to basically literally will be facing the worst of stagflation

recommendations.speaker: David Woo
recommendations.reasoning: US passed massive green energy subsidies bill. Europeans responding with own industrial policy to compete. Europe will increase debt to fund massive subsidies for domestic green energy companies. Companies benefiting from subsidies will be profitable despite sector struggles. Clean energy ETFs were down 30-60% last year.
recommendations.quote: So this is actually a time to actually start looking at European companies that will benefit from a massive increase in subsidies in Europe that are basically going to European companies

recommendations.speaker: David Woo
recommendations.reasoning: China reopening should drive strong increase in car sales. Tesla has been struggling mainly due to slowdown in Chinese car sales. China is world's largest car market with 25M sales vs 15M in US. Reopening will benefit Tesla significantly.
recommendations.quote: that probably should basically benefit Tesla, by the way, because Tesla clearly has been struggling mainly because of the slowdown in car sales in China, which is the biggest market

recommendations.speaker: Markus
recommendations.reasoning: Small Swedish space company with data in space business. Recently received large order of 62 million euros for space cloud. Company not profitable yet but worth monitoring for future years. Space technology sector showing growth.
recommendations.quote: Unibap, which is a smaller Swedish space company, which is like data in space, which recently got a big order for their space cloud, which was I think it was 62 million euros. And even though the company is not profitable at this point, I think it's a company you should be, you should pay attention to it

recommendations.speaker: David Woo
recommendations.reasoning: Swedish housing debt much too high. Market more overvalued than many other countries. Stefan Ingves (who restructured Swedish banking after 90s collapse) has expressed concern. If recession occurs, housing will be hit hard. Recent data shows houses down 3%, apartments down 1% in December.
recommendations.quote: I would stay out of anything housing related... I do think that the Swedish, I think the Swedish basically housing debt is much too high. Now, and from that point of view, the market is more overvalued than many other countries

insights.quote: But what is interesting about what's happening this January is so contrasting to what we went through last year... The market thing, it doesn't really matter what I, you know, what I think. But right now, the market is trading with so much conviction about inflation going down to 2%. The fact that inflation break even trading at 2% tells you the market is not even building any kind of uncertainty premium.
insights.summary: Market conviction on inflation dropping to 2% is extreme - no uncertainty premium being priced. Contrasts with reality of 6.5% current inflation. This consensus view often leads to reversals.
insights.speaker: David Woo

insights.quote: It's actually fascinating because this is why, you know, January trades invariably always blow up in basically February. But I think this assumption that we're going to get a soft lending is so basically preposterous.
insights.summary: January investment trades based on consensus views typically fail by February as reality sets in. Market's soft landing assumption is unrealistic.
insights.speaker: David Woo

insights.quote: Because for them, the playing field was really the global market. They felt that they had invented Sweden, Sweden only after they've understood what's happening in terms of the global basically environment. I think if that was the case 15 years ago, today it has to be like doubly true.
insights.summary: Successful investors must understand global macro environment before analyzing specific companies. Swedish companies are globally exposed, making global awareness essential. This is doubly true today compared to 15 years ago.
insights.speaker: David Woo

insights.quote: So politics is what drives policies, and policies is what drives economics and markets, and economics drives markets. So you have to go all the way back. So you have to understand how this politics drive policies.
insights.summary: Political analysis is critical but overlooked by most investors. Politics drives policies, which drive economics and markets. Must follow news daily to understand causal chain of events.
insights.speaker: David Woo

insights.quote: I don't want people to tell me what this basically fact means. I just want to read the facts basically and inform myself, because if I have lots of facts, then I'm gonna be able to string together the facts and make sense of them myself.
insights.summary: Prefer pure factual reporting over editorialized news. Build understanding by collecting raw facts and connecting them yourself rather than accepting others' interpretations.
insights.speaker: David Woo

insights.quote: So what I'm saying is that at any given point in time, if you know what's important, then you would just follow the important stories, and not waste your time with the less important stories. But to do that, to know what's important, you have to follow the market's narrative.
insights.summary: Focus time on truly important stories rather than noise. Knowing what matters requires understanding current market narrative. Efficient information consumption is critical.
insights.speaker: David Woo

summary: David Woo argues market's soft landing consensus is wrong, expecting higher inflation and Fed hawkishness. Bullish on energy prices due to China reopening (explosive demand growth to 14M barrels/day) and potential Russian offensive in Ukraine. Recommends long June 2023 oil futures (target 100 from 84), hedged with S&P 500 short. Bearish on euro due to Europe's stagflation risk from war and high energy costs. Notes opportunity in European green energy companies receiving subsidies, but warns against Swedish housing due to overvaluation and high debt. Emphasizes importance of political analysis and global macro understanding for investors.
key_takeaways: Market pricing 2% inflation with no uncertainty premium - extreme consensus likely wrong
China reopening will drive explosive oil demand, 2M barrels/day increase with no spare capacity
Russian offensive expected in next 2-3 weeks will spike oil prices and crush Europe
Long oil futures June 2023 (84→100), short S&P 500 as hedge, short euro
European green energy subsidies create investment opportunity
Swedish housing market overvalued with excessive debt - avoid
January trades based on consensus typically fail by February
